comments.content: The `#6892` workaround comment is kept, but the code that performed the truncation was dropped. `std::string(RESOURCEDIR).c_str()` was the idiom that stripped NUL bytes injected into the `-DRESOURCEDIR=...` define; `std::string(RESOURCEDIR)` no longer expresses that intent. comments.content: The new helper does not check the result of `PyErr_NewException`. If it returns `nullptr` (memory error / invalid base), `Py_INCREF(exception)` dereferences a null pointer and crashes during interpreter setup, and a subsequent `PyModule_AddObject` failure is silently ignored while the corresponding `PyExc_FC_*` global stays null (it is used all over the code base afterwards). Consider bailing out early instead of INCREF-ing a possibly-null pointer.

Actually no: a member function definition outside the class must appear in a namespace enclosing the class. Global namespace encloses App, and the name `Application` is found via using-directive...
